Uniqueness must hold across types that correlations may exchange, and old incidences/colors must be reconstructed. The stated extension image is exact.

Deleting the recognizable old set gives subdivided stars with a unique degree-d center and distinct arm lengths. These force ordered positions and pointwise rigidity. Old recognizability remains an explicit hypothesis.
Reduced multiplication cancels only across the factor boundary; the last-i prefix lies entirely in the factor avoiding J. Converse splits at the last occurrence.
The prefix condition is conjunction over omitted labels, including the empty intersection.

Standard right cosets are convex in the left-multiplication Cayley tree. Finite subtree Helly gives common representatives and chamber regularity. Actual residues identify with the smaller free-basis coset geometry; generation gives connectedness.
All basis permutations lift, so the full palette quotient is Sym(I), not merely the exhibited signed subgroup.

After a natural translation a normalizing correlation fixes the chamber. It transports cyclic panel stabilizers, forcing each basis generator to a signed basis generator; the regular chamber action then determines it.
An extension with the fixed natural inner image would inject infinite Out(F) into the finite signed-permutation normalizer quotient. Nielsen powers detected in abelianization prove infinitude.

Replacing only the final i-syllable exponent by an arbitrary permutation of nonzero integers preserves every labeled left-cyclic panel, including complete first-syllable cancellation. Object cosets are exactly reachability classes using other labels. Type-i singleton-power cosets detect faithfulness.

Aut of a finitely generated free group is countable and embeds in the exhibited infinite symmetric subgroup of K. Restricting that embedding to Inn gives the required compatible weak pair, with a different inner image. This does not contradict the natural-image obstruction.
Thinness propagates a type-preserving chamber stabilizer through the connected chamber graph. Chamber transitivity then yields the exact complement. Connectivity is essential.

Types have sizes 2|P|,2|Q|,2|E|; the edge type is recognizable. The exact within-type twin pairs recover the simple bipartite graph and all independent flips. Every flag extends and every panel has two completions. An outer involution in the full doubled group would project to an outer involution of the graph group.

Recognition uses vertex/edge degrees for odd n and class sizes for even n. The affine action is regular on incident vertex-edge pairs; fixing adjacent vertices of the selected Hamiltonian cycle gives the matching upper bound. Unit groups need not be cyclic and geometric completion is distinct from the literal system.
The complete-graph incidence system has the stated pair for n>=4. Classical Aut(Sn) is retained; n=1,2 are explicitly corrected and n=3 separated.

Intersecting duad stars reconstruct S6. Intrinsic involution classes yield Aut(S6) acting faithfully. The reverse conjugation map is faithful because a type-swap centralizing S6 would identify nonconjugate duad/syntheme stabilizers (seven versus three transpositions).

Object class sizes recognize the cube vertices/edges/faces; the whole cube group and even-parity kernel are computed. The central sign-shear identifies the source pair. Adding adjacent opposite-parity vertex incidence repairs chamber existence while preserving that pair; firmness is not claimed.

The twelve Hamiltonian cycles of K5 identify two six-element A5 orbits. The complete six-case table with one cycle fixed gives thirty common-path and six disjoint pairs. Common-edge cross-incidence makes every flag extend and gives120 chambers. Independent-set stars recover S5; Aut(A5)=S5 is retained.

The literal F4 model has105 four-point supports, two new types and twelve orderings in each typed shadow. Thus the pointwise kernel is Sym(12)^210, already too large for PGL(3,4). The same n=3 model is the stated root truncation; Frobenius plus a position swap lifts type-preservingly.

Translations t->t+m give infinitely many outer classes: conjugacy of the displayed diagonal matrices up to scalar is excluded by the eigenvalue of multiplicity n-1>=2. The finite-palette quotient therefore rules out exact representation, but not weak representation or infinite palettes.

Every old q-binomial type has size1 mod p, while every attachment type is divisible by p; this recognizes the old union. Both point and dual pencils are included, so duality preserves the ordered cross-ratio. Distinct arms force unique extensions. Prime-field generation kills precisely the field kernel. The fundamental projective theorem and Aut(PGL) identification are explicit retained classical inputs.
